edges.description: Reduced heme A synthase function restricts synthesis of the complex IV heme cofactor.
Limited heme A compromises maturation and assembly of functional complex IV.
Deficient maturation or activity lowers the functional capacity of terminal respiratory electron transfer.
The cardiac respiratory defect contributes to cardiomyopathy through incompletely resolved intermediates.
Deficient oxidative metabolism is associated with lactate accumulation and acidosis.
Impaired oxidative metabolism can be accompanied by cerebrospinal fluid lactate accumulation; the tissue-level intermediates are not resolved by the clinical report.
Impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism contributes to neurological deterioration; intermediate injury mechanisms remain incompletely resolved.
The neurological phenotype can include bilateral Leigh-pattern lesions.
Severe respiratory dysfunction is associated with disrupted mitochondrial ultrastructure in the muscle model.
Muscle-specific COX15 loss is associated with impaired autophagic clearance; the intervening signaling mechanism is unresolved.
Reduced clearance may permit damaged organelles to accumulate in mouse skeletal muscle.
Patient cells reproduce deficient assembly and partial complementation rescue.
